target_audience_note:
The document states no market segment. It describes itself as "Private Health Insurance
" and "Travel health insurance for journeys abroad", and addresses the reader as the applicant ("your insurance application"). The product name is "BUSINESS TRAVEL", which is a product name and not a statement of audience.
summary: Insurance Product Information Document (IPID) for BUSINESS TRAVEL, described on the page as private health insurance and, in the product-type box, as travel health insurance for journeys abroad. The header band names DKV Luxembourg S.A. as the company. The document lists fourteen benefits in five groups - outpatient treatments, dental treatments, inpatient treatments, ambulance services, and repatriation and return transport - and states that the maximum amounts specified in the General Terms and Conditions of insurance apply to them. Cover is valid for the journey abroad indicated on the insurance application, foreign countries being all territories outside the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the country of permanent residence, and the contract ends automatically on the termination date shown on the policy with no automatic renewal.

gaps:
CARRIER DIVERGENCE BETWEEN THE DOCUMENT AND THE TASK METADATA, and here the document DOES name a carrier. The header band prints "DKV Luxembourg S.A.  -  Product: BUSINESS TRAVEL
" - a named legal entity with its legal form - verified on a 4x render of the band (the header block is printed at the TOP of page 1 at y 35-113 but is emitted LAST in the flat text, so a text-order reader meets it at the end). `insurer_name` therefore records "DKV Luxembourg S.A." and not the task-metadata value "lalux". `insurer_slug` is copied through as "lalux" unchanged, because it is the dataset key supplied by the task. The logo in the top-right corner of the band carries the strapline "membre du Groupe lalux" beneath the DKV Luxembourg wordmark, which is what connects this document to the lalux corpus; that strapline is part of the logo IMAGE and does not exist in the text layer, so it is reported here and deliberately not quoted in `key_quotes` - it could not be grounded. Nothing else in the document mentions lalux: the body refers to the carrier only as "we" / "us" / "our".

Branch: the task metadata gives `sante` and it has been copied through unchanged. The document supports it in its header ("Private Health Insurance
") but its product-type box says "Travel health insurance for journeys abroad", and every benefit and every exclusion is conditioned on a journey abroad, which would also fit the `voyage` slug. The overlap is flagged rather than resolved.

`edition_date` and `reference` are null: no edition date, version code, year, tariff code or printed footer appears on either page. The introductory note refers to "the above-mentioned tariff" but no tariff designation is printed anywhere above it or elsewhere in the document - that dangling reference is itself recorded here rather than resolved. Nothing was promoted from the file name or from PDF file metadata.

Bullet marks are bitmap images, not text and not vector drawings. `page.get_text("text")` returns a bare tab plus space where each mark sits. Membership was recovered from the image blocks of `get_text("dict")`, placed by coordinate, and settled on a render. The arithmetic closes exactly on page 1: 29 image blocks = 14 green ticks (120x133 px, x0 29.8) in "What is insured?
" + 12 red crosses (120x121 px, x0 307.4, y 323.5 to 551.6) in "What is not insured?
" + 3 orange exclamation marks (40x148 px, x0 309.4, y 634.4, 660.8 and 687.2) in "Are there any restrictions on cover?
". Page 2 carries 2 further green ticks (x0 65.1) marking the two items of "Where am I covered?
". Each of the 29 marks is aligned on the baseline of the item it belongs to; no misalignment was observed. The 14 ticks map one-to-one onto the 14 recorded coverages. These counts are stated here and not in `key_quotes`, because image marks are not text and cannot be grounded.

Two-column reversal check run and NEGATIVE. Page 1 is a two-column layout (left column x0 22.7-57.1, right column x0 307.4-334.7). The block order returned by PyMuPDF emits the whole left column before the whole right column and top-to-bottom within each, so the covered benefits, the not-insured items and the restrictions attach to their correct boxes; nothing is crossed. The three polarities are additionally separated by three visually distinct mark types at distinct abscissas. The only flow-order artifact is the full-width header band already described, which carries the carrier name and no coverage or exclusion, so no value is mis-attached.

The "Are there any restrictions on cover?
" box (3 items) has been recorded in `exclusions` alongside the 12 items of the "What is not insured?
" box, because the schema has no separate restrictions array. Each description names the box it came from so the two can be told apart downstream. Note that the third restriction is printed as a lead-in ("Further limitations such as:
") followed by a single indented sub-item about travel warnings; both parts are kept together in one exclusion, and the lead-in's "such as" wording shows the list is open-ended.

NO AMOUNT, sum insured, sub-limit, deductible, waiting period or percentage is printed anywhere in this document. The only quantified statement is the referral "The maximum amounts specified in the General Terms and 
Conditions of insurance apply to the benefits specified.", which is recorded verbatim as the `limits` of every one of the 14 coverages, since the document attaches it to the whole benefit list rather than to any single benefit. `deductibles` is null, `waiting_periods` is empty and `prescription_period` is null: none is mentioned. There is therefore no currency figure in the document at all and no missing-glyph question to settle.

The document declares itself incomplete in two places, and neither statement has been treated as a coverage or an exclusion: "This information sheet is not complete and the examples given below are only an extract of the total benefit catalogue." and "Insurance cover is defined by the type and extent of cover 
described in the General Terms and Conditions of Insurance." The full benefit catalogue is stated to live in the insurance application and offer, the policy and any further stipulated agreement, and the General terms and conditions of insurance GCI. None of those documents was consulted and nothing has been imported from them.

`claims_procedure` is empty: the document contains no claims section and no notification deadline. The three obligations on page 2 concern providing information, submitting to a medical examination and paying premiums; the information and examination duties would apply at claim time but the document does not say so, so no timing has been inferred and `timing` is null on all four obligations.

Printed typography preserved verbatim, not corrected: the country is spelled "Luxemburg" twice in the travel-warning restriction on page 1 and "Luxembourg" on page 2 and in the carrier name; "Grand-Duchy of Luxemburg" on page 1 against "Grand Duchy of Luxembourg" on page 2; "Medical necessary transport using approved rescue services 
to the nearest hospital or doctor" prints "Medical necessary" for "medically necessary"; "The amount of reimbursement is limited on expenses 
incurred.
" prints "limited on" for "limited to"; and the header prints doubled spaces around the dash in "DKV Luxembourg S.A.  -  Product". None has been repaired, so the quotes remain exact spans of the text layer.

One dental benefit is split across a line break with no hyphen ("in order to" / "re-establish ability to chew"); the quote and the coverage description carry the real line break from the text layer rather than a repaired single-line version, so they remain exact spans. The document uses curly quotation marks around "Ministère des affaires étrangères" and one curly apostrophe in "person's pregnancy". Every `key_quotes` entry was sliced programmatically out of the PyMuPDF text layer rather than retyped. No zero-width spaces, no soft hyphens, no Private-Use-Area glyphs and no U+0007 control characters were found in either page.

`definitions` is empty: the document contains no glossary. The sentence "Considered as foreign countries are all territories outside the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the country in which you have 
your permanent residence.
" is the only definition of fact; it is kept in `territorial_scope` and quoted in `key_quotes`.

`target_audience` is null: the product is named BUSINESS TRAVEL and the header says "Private Health Insurance", but the document never states who may buy it - not whether it is sold to entreprises for their travelling staff or to particuliers. The product name was deliberately not converted into an audience category; the document's own wording is kept in `target_audience_note`.
`is_optional` is null on all 14 coverages: the document presents a single benefit list with no formulas, no tiers and no optional add-ons, and never says whether any benefit can be taken separately.

This product is published by the same insurer in several language versions. This document was extracted from its own English text alone; no wording, carrier, date or limit has been taken from a French or German sibling to complete anything here.
